highlights.text: “Remember your promise.” “I will.” “You trusted me with a secret twelve years ago.” “I know.” “I never betrayed you.” “I realize that.” “Now I’m trusting you.”
“In the royal presence, people give their opinions only when asked. And the king almost never asks for the opinions of women.”

“In the last six weeks the king has caused the deaths of thousands of men, women, and children, and burned their crops and their homes. And I have tried to save a twelve-year-old girl from being married to a murderer. Tell me again, Lord William, which of us is mad?”
It was a decision that required long and careful thought, obviously. He made up his mind in a few moments. He was going home.
“If you stay at home, you can’t go to church. Holiness is the best medicine.”

“The plague has been sent by God to punish us for our sins. The world has become wicked. Heresy, lasciviousness, and disrespect are rife. Men question authority, women flaunt their bodies, children disobey their parents. God is angry, and His rage is fearsome. Don’t try to run from His justice! It will find you, no matter where you hide.”
“This plague,” she said. “It’s like a wolf in the forest. When you see it, you don’t think—you run.”
“You are monks, and it is your duty to obey,” he said. “And now let us pray.”
“It is a sin to seek our own death.” “But if death comes to us in the course of our holy duty, we embrace it gladly.”
As it was in the beginning Is now And ever shall be World without end. Amen.
the passage of time, and how it can change an innocent, beloved baby into a man who commits murder.
No one knew better than he how the machinery of justice could fail: after all, he himself had escaped hanging twice.
